To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

end-to-end attention based speech recognition systems can be trained to achieve recognition accuracy similar to that of hybrid HMM based systems, but without the need for explicit alignment of the acoustic features with the phoneme or word sequences.

(1) the attention based RNN is a viable alternative to Connectionist Temporal Classi cation (CTC) based sequence modelling; (2) the attention based approach can be used to integrate a neural decoder with a n gram language model; (3) the attention mechanism can be constrained to improve the efficiency of the decoding process; (4) the attention based decoder can be sped up by using a pooling operation that reduces the length of the source sequence.
we can obtain state of the art recognition results on the WSJ task without HMMs and without CTC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the development and evaluation of an end to end attention based speech recognition system.
the following: 1) How to integrate the decoding RNN and the language model 2) How to speed up the decoding process 3) How to improve the recognition performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed model is a promising alternative to the CTC model and can be used in the context of LVCSR.
the attention based RNN approach is a promising alternative to Connectionist Temporal Clasification based approaches for LVCSR.
the proposed model is able to achieve competitive results with the current state-of-the-art end-to-end models, and is able to achieve a significant improvement over the baseline model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to achieve a word error rate of 13.5\% with a single RNN model on the Wall Street Journal task.
we are able to achieve a 6. 5% relative WER reduction over the state of the art end to end attention based model on the WSJ corpus.
we show how to apply an attention based RNN to a large vocabulary task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
end to end models based on attention mechanisms can provide competitive recognition accuracies and are a viable alternative to Connectionist Temporal classification.
the proposed attention based approach is more efficient than the CTC approach and that it can be easily combined with a language model.
the attention mechanism can be applied to a wide range of sequence modelling problems and can be used to train RNNs for LVCSR without Connectionist Temporal Classiﬁcation. 1.
